correctness.rationale: For indexed linear words avoiding both 000 and 111, a code is precisely a clique in the graph joining words with disjoint arbitrary one-deletion shadows. The output set must include descendants outside the run-limited source; both exact implementations do so. The branching takes each possible highest remaining vertex and then restricts to its neighbors; a proper coloring of each remaining prefix bounds any extension by its number of colors. This proves the soundness of exhaustion with pruning. A fresh standard-library implementation with a different coloring order reproduces the exact optima (1,2,2,3,3,6,6,10,13) and maximum ordinary VT intersections (1,2,2,3,3,6,6,10,12), with 110 permissible inputs at n=9 and residues (11,10,12,12,10,11,10,12,12,10). It checks the explicit thirteen-word code directly. For the classical VT property, on inserting bit b at slot i of a common descendant y, the checksummed integer increases by i b plus the suffix weight of y starting at i. For b=0 and b=1 these increases lie in the disjoint ranges 0 through wt(y) and wt(y)+1 through n. Within either range repeated increases can only come from moving the inserted bit through a run of identical bits, producing the same word. Thus the residue intersections really are codes, and the first strict gap is at nine.
residual_risks: The exact clique enumeration is the finite upper certificate; the package's numerical MILP result is corroborative only. No longer lengths or other run constraints are asserted.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A lower bound on a VT intersection supplies no upper bound on the constrained optimum. An unrestricted optimum bounds a restricted one but does not identify it or show that restricting an optimal unrestricted class remains optimal. Neither line of results settles the length-nine comparison.

A zero-gap constraint with singleton one-runs and guarded endpoints is not an equivalent source under symbol complementation, and NRZI for a constrained encoder does not itself transfer an exact deletion optimum.

value.rationale: Intersecting a VT class with a maximum-run-limited source is a published, natural construction for constrained deletion channels. The first length at which this method cannot be optimal is an informative boundary: the gain of one codeword changes the optimality verdict, with an explicit alternative code and an exact upper bound. This is a small-length benchmark for constrained-code constructions, not a general asymptotic claim.
residual_risks: No claim about the size or frequency of gaps at larger lengths, or about constrained encoding complexity.
